source_title: Navigate360 Data Breach Investigation: Edelson Lechtzin LLP Probes Class Action Claims After Millions of School Tip-Line Records Are Exposed - PR Newswire
source_excerpt:
National class action law firm offers free, confidential case evaluations to individuals whose information may have been exposed in the Navigate360 data breach.
NEWTOWN, Pa. , Oct. 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Edelson Lechtzin LLP , a national class action law firm, is investigating data privacy claims arising from a data breach at Navigate360, a Richfield, Ohio-based school and public safety technology company that provides safety software and anonymous tip-reporting platforms to schools, police agencies, and other organizations. Anyone who received a breach notice or believes their information may have been exposed can request a free case evaluation .
On October 23, 2026, Navigate360 issued a public Notice of Data Breach. The company said it became aware of suspicious activity on one of its systems on or about March 18, 2026. An investigation conducted with a cybersecurity firm determined that an unauthorized third party accessed a system and obtained copies of certain data between November 21, 2025 and March 5, 2026 â a window of more than three months. The company then hired a data-mining firm to review the copied files and determined that some may contain personal information.
Navigate360's products include an anonymous tip-reporting platform that students, families, and the public use to report safety concerns. News coverage reported that roughly 8.3 million tip records were taken, and Nevada officials said the incident reached SafeVoice Nevada, the state's anonymous school tip line, compromising about 10 percent of tips submitted between November 2025 and March 2026 that contained personal information, including student information. Navigate360's notice does not state how many individuals were affected, and it has not published the total number. The company said it has no evidence the information was misused for fraud or identity theft , that it implemented mitigation measures and strengthened its safeguards, and that it reported the matter to law enforcement and notified regulators.
According to Navigate360, the personal information involved may include:
Email addresses and other sensitive information
Navigate360 has said the information involved varies from one individual to the next. Nevada officials have also cited student identification numbers and information related to medical conditions or treatment among the affected tip-line data.
Because the impact depends on what a given record contained, the public notice alone cannot determine whether a person is affected. People who used a Navigate360 tip line, people who were named in a tip, and people whose school or agency used the company's products may all be affected and should watch for a notice letter in the mail. The incident has also been linked to Crime Stoppers programs in the United States and Canada that used the same platform.
Edelson Lechtzin LLP is investigating a potential class action on behalf of individuals whose data may have been compromised. A successful case could recover compensation for losses such as lost time, out-of-pocket costs, and loss of privacy, and could press Navigate360 to strengthen its data protection. The firm evaluates claims at no cost.
Watch for any mail from Navigate360 and keep it, along with any enrollment details for the protection services it offers.
Place a free fraud alert or credit freeze with Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion, and obtain your free reports at AnnualCreditReport.com.
Review your bank, card, and insurance statements for anything you do not recognize, and report suspected identity theft to the Federal Trade Commission at IdentityTheft.gov.
